mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 8% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the 20-day periods after UNRATE exceeds 8%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP and housing starts indicates strong demand, which may boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods following simultaneous GDP and housing growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 3% in a late-cycle expansion may indicate supply chain resilience, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day periods during late-cycle expansion with industrial production growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the 5-day periods following payroll increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A $10 billion increase in real state and local government purchases indicates increased demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 20-day periods following RSAFS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates combined with high unemployment rates may indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods with low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates during a monetary tightening cycle may lead to increased borrowing costs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods during monetary tightening, the hypothesis is rejected.
